cls: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (non-steroidal oral contraceptive)
pharm: Non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator; weekly oral contraceptive with anti-estrogenic action on the endometrium.
quick: 30 mg twice weekly x12 weeks, then 30 mg once weekly (contraception)
May be taken with or without food, on fixed weekdays
Menstrual pattern, pregnancy exclusion, ovarian cysts
summary: Ormeloxifene (Centchroman) is a non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator developed in India and used as a once-weekly oral contraceptive; it is also used for dysfunctional uterine bleeding/menorrhagia. It acts as an anti-estrogen on the endometrium (causing asynchrony between endometrial development and ovulation) while having mixed estrogen agonist/antagonist effects elsewhere. It is NOT FDA-approved; dosing and indications follow Indian regulatory/manufacturer information. Common effects include delayed/prolonged menstrual cycles and a risk of ovarian cyst formation.
indications: (Investigated for advanced breast cancer and other estrogen-sensitive conditions)

dosage.d: 30 mg twice weekly for first 12 weeks, then 30 mg once weekly
dosage.n: Start on day 1 of cycle; take on the same two/one weekday(s); maintain weekly thereafter

dosage.d: 60 mg twice weekly for 12 weeks, then 60 mg once weekly for 12 weeks

admin: Take on fixed days of the week to maintain the weekly schedule
For contraception, begin on the first day of menstruation
May be taken with or without food
Use a backup method during the first few weeks until the regimen is established
moa: Non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator with tissue-specific estrogen agonist and antagonist activity; its anti-estrogenic effect on the endometrium delays endometrial proliferation and creates asynchrony between endometrial maturation and ovulation, impairing implantation and providing contraception, while reducing excessive endometrial growth in menorrhagia.

absolute: Known or suspected breast or genital malignancy (estrogen-dependent)

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy; discontinue immediately if pregnancy is confirmed or suspected.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding; avoid use in lactating women.
renal: Use with caution; contraindicated in severe renal disease. Limited pharmacokinetic data in impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in hepatic disease or jaundice; the drug undergoes hepatic metabolism.

moderate: Enzyme-inducing drugs (e.g., rifampicin, certain anticonvulsants) - may theoretically reduce efficacy
Other estrogen-modulating agents - effects may overlap
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: Exclude pregnancy if menstrual cycles become markedly delayed; evaluate persistent pelvic symptoms for ovarian cysts.

emergency: Acute abdomen from ovarian cyst complication (rupture/torsion)

monitoring: Pregnancy testing if cycles are significantly delayed (>2 weeks)
Symptoms suggesting ovarian cysts (pelvic pain, bloating)
counsel: Take it on the same fixed day(s) each week to stay protected
Your periods may become less frequent or delayed - this is expected; tell your doctor if a period is more than 2 weeks late
Use a backup contraceptive method during the first weeks
Report severe pelvic pain or a missed period to exclude pregnancy/ovarian cyst
Do not use if you are or might be pregnant
pk: Contraceptive efficacy builds over the initial weeks
Plasma peak within hours of dosing
Long, approximately 168 hours (~7 days), supporting weekly dosing
Store at room temperature; protect from moisture and light
pearls: Not FDA-approved; developed and marketed in India (Saheli/Chhaya) - dosing follows Indian regulatory/manufacturer information, not a US/openFDA label
A non-steroidal, non-hormonal weekly contraceptive SERM - distinctive among oral contraceptives
Long half-life (~1 week) allows once-weekly maintenance dosing
Cycle lengthening/delayed menses is common and expected - exclude pregnancy if very late
Watch for ovarian cyst formation; contraindicated in PCOD, hepatic disease, and pregnancy
missed: If a scheduled weekly dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, take that dose and resume the regular schedule. Use a backup contraceptive method if doses are missed, and do not double up.
overdose: Specific overdose data are limited. Manage supportively; there is no specific antidote. Monitor for exaggerated anti-estrogenic effects and gynecologic symptoms.
refs: Note: not FDA-approved; verify against current local product information and gynecology guidance
